text:
Tage Thompson changed positions this season and the goals came with him: 10 in 17 games, including a three-goal, five-point night in Anaheim and two more in Los Angeles the next game. Buffalo's coverage has started floating the 50-goal mark, and he has the tool for it. His hardest shot this season, 100.2 mph, tops the league's tracking.

The chances back it up. He is generating 1.40 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, a touch above last season, and he is shooting 14.3%, right in his normal range. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile of forwards at getting to the home-plate area in front of the net. The soft spot is around him: Buffalo has scored 6.5 more goals than expected with him on the ice, and the team gets just under half of the five-on-five chances when he plays.

Our projection says about 42 goals, which leaves 50 as a reach rather than a pace. Watch whether the position change keeps him in the slot when the power play cools.
headline: Thompson, a new position and the hardest shot
